title: Bus on-time performance decline at Corrin Valley Transit

organization.size: approx. 1,250 staff including 940 bus operators; 310 buses on 38 routes run from two garages (North Garage, South Garage)

presentingRequest: Our bus on-time performance has dropped from 82% to 71% since the spring, and the board wants it fixed. The cause is clear to me: operator absenteeism is up 40%. When operators don't show, we scramble for extraboard drivers, pull-outs go out late and spare operators who don't know the routes run behind all day. We want your help rolling out a tougher attendance program - progressive discipline starting at three recorded absence occurrences in 90 days - and a communications plan for the union. - Marcus Whitfield, Director of Bus Operations

evidence.text: "Absences went up 40% starting in April, and on-time performance fell off a cliff in the same month. That's not a coincidence. Every call-off means an extraboard operator who may not know the route, or a bus held at the garage while dispatch finds someone. The spring service change was routine - Scheduling tells me the running times are fine. And the road work is the city's problem; it's a few blocks, it can't move a whole network."

evidence.source: Monthly on-time performance report to the Board (Service Performance unit, 2026-10-02)
evidence.text: Systemwide on-time performance (OTP), weekday: Jan 82.4%, Feb 81.9%, Mar 82.1%, Apr 76.8%, May 72.3%, Jun 71.0%, Jul 70.4%, Aug 70.9%, Sep 70.6%. Definition: a timepoint departure counts as on time if it is between 1 minute early and 5 minutes late, measured by the automatic vehicle location (AVL) system at every timepoint on every operated trip. Trips that are not operated are excluded from OTP and reported separately as missed trips. The OTP definition and the AVL equipment have not changed since 2023.

evidence.source: HR monthly attendance report, bus operators (2026-10-01)
evidence.text: Operator absence occurrences per month: Jan 598, Feb 621, Mar 617 (average 612); Apr 832, May 861, Jun 849, Jul 874, Aug 866, Sep 860 (average 857). Change: +40%. Headcount of operators stable at 930-945 throughout.

"The absence board is longer every morning than I've ever seen it. We use the extraboard every day, and some mornings I've held a pull-out ten minutes while I find somebody. Extraboard operators cover whatever is open - any route out of this garage, there's no preference by route."

"The spring pick cut our layovers to nothing. On the 9 you hit the end of the line late and you turn straight around, no bathroom, no break, and you're late the whole next trip. Management blames absences, but half of what's on that board is people who went home sick at two in the afternoon. We filed a schedule grievance in May; nobody answered."

evidence.source: Spring 2026 service change summary (Scheduling department, effective Sunday 2026-04-05)
evidence.text: To operate new Route 51 without adding buses, recovery (layover) time was reduced on 21 of 38 routes, from a median of 15% of round-trip running time to 8%. Scheduled running times between timepoints were not changed on any route. The other 17 routes (including all 6 express routes) kept their previous recovery time and running times. Nine buses were freed for Route 51.

evidence.source: City of Corrin Public Works construction notice (published 2026-03-12)
evidence.text: Halvorsen Avenue water-main replacement and Bridgeport Road bridge rehabilitation: lane reductions to one lane each direction begin 2026-04-20, expected to last until August 2027. Transit routes using these corridors: 9, 14 and 22 (Halvorsen Avenue); 31 and 33 (Bridgeport Road). [Scheduling note appended: all five of these routes are among the 21 routes whose recovery time was reduced on 2026-04-05.]

Weekday OTP, Jan-Mar vs Jun-Sep 2026. Group A - 5 construction-corridor routes, recovery cut (24% of scheduled trips): 83.5% -> 52.5%. Group B - 16 routes with recovery cut, no construction (36% of trips): 81.6% -> 71.5%. Group C - 17 routes with no recovery cut and no construction (40% of trips): 82.3% -> 81.7%. Group A accounts for 39% of all not-on-time trips in Jun-Sep (22% in Jan-Mar). Weekly series: Groups A and B both step down in the week of 2026-04-06; Group A steps down a second, larger time in the week of 2026-04-20; Group C shows no step in either week. Groups A, B and C each include routes from both garages.

PM-peak median running time through the 2.1 km Halvorsen Avenue work zone: 6.5 min before 2026-04-20, 13.0 min after. Bridgeport Road work-zone segment: 4.0 min before, 9.5 min after. Running times on the non-corridor segments of the same five routes are unchanged (within 0.3 min).

Share of trips leaving their first timepoint more than 5 minutes late. Group B: 6% (Jan-Mar) -> 19% (Jun-Sep). Group C: 6% -> 7%. On Group B, 81% of these late first-timepoint departures came after the same bus's inbound trip arrived less than 3 minutes before the scheduled departure time; the bus was present and an operator was on board.
Average weekday boardings: Jan-Mar 61,200; Jun-Sep 60,400. Median dwell time per serviced stop: 18 seconds in both periods. Wheelchair-ramp deployments per day: 212 vs 208.

evidence.source: Quality Assurance manual ride checks, Q2 2026 (QA unit, 2026-07-15)
evidence.text: Checkers rode 96 randomly selected trips and recorded 412 timepoint departures by stopwatch. Manual result agreed with the AVL on-time/not-on-time classification at 97% of timepoints. Manual OTP for the sample: 72%; AVL OTP for the same trips: 73%.

evidence.source: IT project close-out report, ShiftLine timekeeping system (2026-06-30)
evidence.text: ShiftLine went live for all operators on 2026-03-30, replacing paper sign-in sheets and supervisor-entered absence codes. Under the legacy process an absence occurrence was entered only when an operator missed an entire assignment; partial-day absences (reporting more than 10 minutes late, leaving early, mid-shift relief for illness) were handled by a supervisor note and not entered as occurrences. ShiftLine automatically records every such partial-day absence as an occurrence.

evidence.source: HR re-analysis of absence occurrences by type (HR analyst, 2026-10-20)
evidence.text: Apr-Sep average 857 occurrences/month = 619 full-day absences + 238 partial-day absences. Jan-Mar average 612 occurrences/month, all full-day (no partial-day category existed). Full-day absences: +1.1%. Partial-day entries account for 238 of the 245-occurrence monthly increase.

evidence.source: Dispatch log, both garages (Dispatch supervisor export, 2026-10-21)
evidence.text: This log is kept by dispatchers and is independent of ShiftLine; its procedure has not changed since 2022. Trips not operated because no operator was available: Jan-Mar 0.7% of scheduled trips (average 412/month); Apr-Sep 0.7% (average 405/month). Garage pull-outs more than 2 minutes late: 3.1% vs 3.3%. Extraboard assignments per day, including mid-shift reliefs: 41 vs 43.

evidence.source: HR breakdown of partial-day early-leave occurrences by operator assignment and garage, Apr-Sep 2026 (HR analyst, 2026-10-20)
evidence.text: Early-leave occurrences per 100 operators per month, by the operator's regular (picked) assignment, both garages pooled: operators on recovery-cut routes 18; operators on other routes 10. By garage: North 19, South 11 (North operates 15 of the 21 recovery-cut routes; South operates 6). Assignments are picked by seniority, so operators on recovery-cut routes are older on average (48 vs 42 years), and the recovery-cut routes include most of the network's longest routes. No pre-April early-leave data exist for comparison, because the legacy process did not record early leaves.

"I've seen the HR breakdown. A partial day is still an absence - if you leave early, someone else has to cover you. The attendance policy counts every occurrence ShiftLine records, and I intend to take it to the board next month as planned."

hypotheses.text: The increase in operator absenteeism is the main driver of the decline in on-time performance.
Operators are failing to work their assigned work materially more often than before April 2026; the 40% rise in absence occurrences reflects a real change in attendance.
The shortened recovery (layover) time introduced in the April 2026 service change is a major contributor to late trips on the affected routes.
Road construction on Halvorsen Avenue and Bridgeport Road is a major contributor to late trips on the routes using those corridors.
Growing ridership and longer stop dwell times are driving the decline in on-time performance.
The on-time performance decline is a measurement artifact of the reporting system rather than a real change in bus punctuality.

edges.from: Rise in recorded operator absence occurrences (from April 2026)
Reduction of recovery (layover) time on 21 routes
edges.to: Increase in late trips on those routes

edges.from: Lane reductions on Halvorsen Avenue and Bridgeport Road
edges.to: Increase in late trips on the five corridor routes
Operators leaving shifts early (partial-day early-leave absences)

edges.from: Introduction of the ShiftLine timekeeping system
edges.to: Rise in recorded operator absence occurrences

actions.text: Adopt the proposed attendance program: progressive discipline beginning at three absence occurrences in 90 days, counting every occurrence recorded in the timekeeping system.
Make an off-cycle schedule adjustment restoring recovery time on the routes where it was cut, starting with the worst-performing routes.

Set construction-period running times for the five corridor routes and work with Public Works on work-zone traffic management (e.g., signal timing, temporary stop placement) for the duration of the lane reductions.

Restate the operator absence trend separating full-day from partial-day occurrences, and annotate the attendance report with any changes in how absences are recorded, before any attendance-policy decision.
Suspend publication of on-time performance figures to the Board and the public until the measurement system has been audited.

evidenceRequests.text: Dispatch log of trips not operated for lack of an operator and extraboard usage, January-September 2026
Documentation of changes to timekeeping or absence-recording procedures in 2026, with absence occurrences broken down by type
AVL on-time performance by route and week, before and after April 2026
On-time performance benchmarks for peer transit agencies of similar size
Individual attendance histories of the 20 operators with the most absence occurrences
